confidences.reason: Yes, the agent incorrectly ruled out green edges. The given facts only guarantee: all blue pieces; orange center and its four adjacent edges (including orange–green); all green corners; all green–yellow edges; and, for each found orange piece, the opposite red piece (including red–green). These do not account for the green–white edge, so concluding the missing edge could not involve green was unjustified.

In Step 1, the Cubing_Expert incorrectly infers that the missing edge cannot involve green because "all blue and green pieces" were found. The given conditions only guarantee all blue pieces, all green corners, and green pieces bordering yellow—this does not include the green–white edge. Thus, Step 1 prematurely eliminates the correct candidate (green–white) and steers the reasoning toward red–white. This is the earliest substantive mistake leading to the wrong outcome.

The Cubing_Expert concluded the missing piece was red–white without adequately reconsidering green edges, and the Verification_Expert endorsed this conclusion twice (Steps 2 and 4) without re-evaluating the green-edge constraints. No subsequent step corrected or challenged this, and the session terminated.
